10.1002_adfm.202516637: To simplify synthetic strategies of hangman porphyrins is critical toward efficient and scalable electrochemical nitrate (NO 3 ‾) reduction reaction (NO 3 ‾RR) to ammonia (NH 3 ) for sustainable nitrogen cycle management, which remains challenging. In this work, a noncovalent assembled method is developed to in situ embed iron tetraphenylporphyrin (FeTPP) inside a robust polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) based hydrogel. The significant pendant hydroxyl groups of PVA established a hangman configuration toward the embedded FeTPP. In situ infrared absorption spectroscopy and theoretical calculations indicated that the formed hangman configuration enables dual‐site cooperative catalysis, that the Fe sites selectively bind to the *NO 2 intermediate emerged in the potential determining step of NO 3 ‾RR, while the pendant hydroxyl groups simultaneously exhibited electron donation to the intermediate, which facilitated the *NO 2 hydrogenation and overall NO 3 ‾RR thermodynamics. Such a catalytic mode delivered a high NH 3 yield rate of 52.4 mg mg cat −1 h −1 under industrially relevant continuous‐flow electrofiltration conditions in neutral media. These findings demonstrate a mechanistically rational and scalable strategy for the synthesis of hangman porphyrins electrocatalysts, and bridged molecular design with electrochemical NH 3 production from NO 3 ‾‐laden wastewater.
10.1002_adfm.75813: 3D printed micro‐supercapacitors have attracted unprecedented attention in the fields of wearable electronics and Internet of Things devices. However, the conventional electrode materials generally suffer from limited porous structure and insufficient active sites, resulting in low specific capacitance and restricted practical application. In this work, we report a 3D printed micro‐supercapacitor based on a heterostructured COF@MOF‐Ti 3 C 2 T x electrode material, which features an engineered nanoporous structure and high electrochemical activity. Due to the precise control of hierarchical nanopores and active cobalt and nickel metal sites, enhanced redox activity, the COF@MOF‐Ti 3 C 2 T x electrode material has fast ion diffusion kinetics, high ion adsorption energy, excellent electron conductivity, and large pseudocapacitive reversibility. As a result, COF@MOF‐Ti 3 C 2 T x achieves a high capacitance of 1078.0 F g −1 , a lower ionic diffusion impedance and structural stability. Furthermore, the assembled solid‐state micro‐supercapacitor exhibits an energy density of 60.3 µWh cm −2 and cyclic stability for successfully powering intelligent traffic signals and alarm clocks, which provides a new approach for the development of high‐performance and customizable micro‐energy storage systems.
10.1021_acsami.6c09852: The electrochemical performance of CVD graphene electrodes has remained inconsistent and often inferior to that of exfoliated graphene, limiting their utility in analytical applications. This variability is widely attributed to structural disorder, but the dominant source remains unclear. Here, we show that amorphous carbon contamination introduced during synthesis is the primary factor governing the electrochemical behavior of CVD graphene. By eliminating this disorder during growth through oxygen-free CVD (OF-CVD), we obtain graphene electrodes that exhibit intrinsic and highly reproducible electrochemical behavior. Compared with conventional and commercial graphene, these electrodes display substantially enhanced heterogeneous electron-transfer kinetics, reduced charge-transfer resistance, and improved detection limits across both outer- and inner-sphere redox systems. Notably, they exhibit consistent anodic peak potentials across wide concentration ranges, nearly eliminating the concentration-dependent potential shifts characteristic of both glassy carbon and commercial/contaminated graphene electrodes. Further, microelectrode array architectures fabricated from this material suppress non-Faradaic background currents and exhibit steady-state diffusion behavior consistent with electrochemical theory, with improved signal-to-noise ratios. Together, these results establish that extrinsic carbon disorder has limited the electrochemical performance of CVD graphene to date. The removal of amorphous carbon reveals defect-free graphene's intrinsic electrochemical behavior and enables a reproducible, high-performance electrode platform, providing a clear pathway for reliable graphene-based electrochemical systems.
10.1038_s41467-025-66795-5: H 2 S reversibly modifies low molecular weight (L MW SH) and protein (PrSH) thiols to form persulfides (RSS − ) and polysulfides (RS(S) n S − ) for antioxidant defence and regulation of activity. However, our understanding of the biological significance of these processes is hampered by our inability to quantify these modifications. We develop a sensitive LC-MS/MS procedure that traps the sulfur atom of H 2 S, and the terminal sulfur atom of RSS − and RS(S) n S − as diagnostic products in biological samples. In parallel, we also trap internal S atoms of RS(S) n S − , enabling quantification of H 2 S, RSS − and RS(S) n S − . L MW S(S) n S − and PrS(S) n S − are determined simultaneously in the same sample. Glutathione (GSH) is the most abundant L MW SH so we develop an orthogonal approach to quantify GSS − , enabling corroboration of L MW SS − measurements by sulfur atom trapping. We demonstrate in systems from proteins to ex vivo tissues how these approaches enable exploration of persulfidation in biological systems.

10.1080_19475705.2026.2660866: Floods cause severe global damage, demanding smarter, data-driven solutions. Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) integrated with Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPT) is advancing flood disaster management through intelligent automation, data fusion, and adaptive geospatial analysis. This study systematically reviews 130 selected papers from a large initial pool using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, providing a comprehensive assessment of methodologies and technologies in flood mapping and hydrological modeling. A quantitative synthesis shows that approximately 45–50% of studies employ machine learning ensembles, 25–30% deep learning models, 18–22% physically based approaches, and only 3–5% explore GPT-based techniques. Based on these insights, FloodMapGPT is introduced as a conceptual, forward-looking framework to demonstrate how GeoAI and GPT technologies can be systematically integrated into future flood-mapping and decision-support systems. The framework enables natural language interaction with geospatial data, facilitating automated report generation and flood analysis. Furthermore, this study outlines key opportunities, challenges, and future research directions, emphasizing the need to adapt GPT for spatial reasoning and geospatial intelligence to support next-generation flood management systems.
